I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou best. In my place, this is the most familiar pattern, the easiest to manage with machines, and the safest for income and food grain. I will not put much land into cotton or other cash crops because I am 56, I want work I can finish on time, and I do not want a crop that needs more picking, more sprays, and more labor. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable emergence and steady yield, not seed-saving risk. For wheat, I will feed it more water and more nitrogen because our winter and spring are dry, and wheat is the crop that usually needs the tighter management here. For maize, I will rely more on summer rain, keep irrigation light, and use less pesticide unless pressure becomes obvious. I will plough before wheat to reset the field well, then I will go with no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest so I can sow fast, save moisture, and reduce labor. My goal is not the absolute highest yield; my goal is a dependable crop I can manage cleanly through the whole year. This matches the common Quzhou pattern of winter wheat and summer maize reported for the county and the wider North China Plain: [Ministry of Agriculture report](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202107/t20210720_6372348.htm), [PMC study on Quzhou wheat-maize rotation](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7988609/), [MDPI county study](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/13/9/2362).
